Source: [src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/BacktestStrategyBase.cs:9](../../../../src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/BacktestStrategyBase.cs#L9).

Convenience base class for IBacktestStrategy implementations. Every callback is a virtual no-op, so a strategy only overrides the events it actually cares about instead of providing an empty stub for each of the eight interface members. Only Name is abstract, since a strategy has no sensible default identifier.

## FillConservatism

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk.FillConservatism</code>. Kind: `enum`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/ExecutionRealism.cs:29](../../../../src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/ExecutionRealism.cs#L29).

Controls how optimistic the bar-based fill models are about limit and stop executions.

```csharp
public enum FillConservatism
```

Enum declarations:

| Declaration | Source | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>Conservative</code> | [src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/ExecutionRealism.cs:45](../../../../src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/ExecutionRealism.cs#L45) | Conservative limit/stop semantics (default): A resting limit order fills at the bar open when the bar opens through the limit, and otherwise requires the bar to trade strictly through the limit price — a bare touch does not fill (queue-position risk). A stop-market order fills no better than its stop price: the fill base is max(stop, open) for buys and min(stop, open) for sells, so gaps through the stop fill at the (worse) opening price, with slippage applied on top. A stop-limit order newly triggered inside a bar fills at the worst in-range price permitted by its limit, and does not fill at all on the trigger bar when the bar opened beyond the limit. |
| <code>Optimistic</code> | [src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/ExecutionRealism.cs:53](../../../../src/Meridian.Backtesting.Sdk/ExecutionRealism.cs#L53) | Legacy optimistic semantics: limit orders fill at the limit price on a bare touch of the bar range, and triggered stop-market orders execute at the bar midpoint, which can be a better price than the stop itself. Runs using this mode are flagged in the bias-disclosure report. |
